description: The figure is a two-level donut (sunburst) chart showing how items are distributed across four inner “layers” and their corresponding outer subcategories. The inner ring contains 4 slices with percentage labels: Semantic Layer (41.2%, medium blue), Perception Layer (40.4%, darker blue), Cultural Layer (14.1%, light gray), and Signal Layer (4.3%, dark slate/blue). The outer ring breaks these into 13 labeled sub-slices: for the Semantic Layer, Content Analysis (large light-blue segment), Emotion & Intention (small light-blue segment), and Speaker Analysis (small light-blue segment); for the Perception Layer, Environmental Perception & Reasoning (large blue segment), Counting & Statistics (medium blue segment), Music Theory (medium blue segment), Correlation Analysis (smaller blue segment), Temporal Analysis (small blue segment), and Spatial Analysis (small blue segment); for the Cultural Layer, Professional Knowledge & Reasoning (light-gray segment), Culture of Speaker (light-gray segment), and Aesthetic Analysis (light-gray segment); and for the Signal Layer, Anomaly Detection (very thin dark segment) and Acoustic Quality Analysis (very thin dark segment). A legend is not shown; labels are placed directly on slices, with percentages shown only on the inner ring, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized; the outer segments visually follow the circular order of their parent inner slice rather than an obvious global size-sorted order.
